title: First-Fitting preparation and affine lci charts on the smooth complement of a pure curve
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a scheme locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$ be the first-Fitting singular subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme], and let $V$ be the locus of points of $C$ that have an open neighbourhood smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $V=|C|\setminus i(|Z|)$. Moreover, every $x\in V$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq V$ in $C$ with $A$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra that is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. No nodality or unramifiedness assumption on $Z$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci), proof: the first-Fitting complement is smooth and is a local complete intersection; use Divisors Tag 0C3K (lemma-d-fitting-ideal-omega-smooth) with its flatness, finite-presentation and fibre-dimension hypotheses verified over a field.

proof.text: The only ideals of $k$ are $(0)$ and $(1)$: if an ideal contains $a\ne0$, it contains $a^{-1}a=1$. Both ideals are finitely generated, so $k$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The single affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}k$ therefore makes the base locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth].

Apply [lem-pc-flat-field] to $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to obtain flatness. Since $f$ is locally of finite type and the base is locally Noetherian by Step 1, [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] gives that $f$ is locally of finite presentation. These assertions do not require $C$ to be quasi-compact or separated.

source.place: Tag 01TX (lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation), part (1); flatness over a field is the field specialization used in curves.tex, Tag 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci).

proof.text: The base $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is integral and its sole point $\eta$ is generic, with residue field $k$. Thus the generic-fibre projection $C_\eta=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k\to C$ is the identity up to its canonical isomorphism. In particular its image is all of $C$ and hence dense, and each of its irreducible components has dimension $1$ by the hypothesis on $C$. Apply [lem-trf-flat-dense-generic-fibre-pure-dimension] with $X=C$, this $S$, and $d=1$, using Step 2 for flatness and the given local finite type. Its geometric-fibre clause shows that every nonempty geometric fibre of $f$ is equidimensional of dimension $1$. This also covers empty $C$ vacuously.

source.place: Tag 0GSK (remark-flat-equidimensional), second list specialized to a field; morphisms.tex, Tag 02NK (lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-dth-fitting-smooth-locus] to $f$ with $d=1$. Flatness and local finite presentation are Step 2, and the required pure geometric fibres are Step 3. Its smooth locus is exactly the set $V$ of the statement, defined by smooth open neighbourhoods, and is open. By [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme] its closed subscheme $Z_1$ is the given $Z$, since both are cut out by $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega^1_{C/k})$. The conclusion $|Z_1|=|C|\setminus V$ therefore gives $V=|C|\setminus i(|Z|)$.

source.place: Tag 0C3K (lemma-d-fitting-ideal-omega-smooth), with d=1; curves.tex, Tag 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci), proof on the complement of Z.

proof.text: Fix $x\in V$. Choose a smooth open neighbourhood $W$ of $x$ as in the definition of $V$. The affine-local characterization included in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] says that smooth morphisms are given locally by smooth ring maps. Applied to $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ at $x$, it supplies an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $W$ containing $x$, with $k\to A$ smooth. Here the nonempty affine target chart is all of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Every point of $W$ has the smooth open neighbourhood $W$, so $W\subseteq V$; hence $U$ is an affine open of $C$ contained in $V$. By [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], $A$ has a presentation $k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ and is therefore finitely generated over $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-local-complete-intersection] to this smooth $k$-algebra $A$. It is a local complete intersection over $k$, as required. None of these arguments uses nodality or any condition on $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.
